`Refunder.refund` (src/refunds.ts) exists to give customers refunds, and to stop those refunds being used to drain money. I took this from `ostf context` and the code. I didn't run any tests, and I haven't changed any files.

## Why it exists
It implements three requirements. All three trace to the need **N-REFUNDS**: "Customers get refunds quickly without the business losing money to abuse."

- **R-REFUND-ORIGINAL** (the `@req` tag on the method): a refund goes back to the payment method of the charge it refunds, never to another one. The method looks up the receipt and calls `gateway.refund(receipt.txn, amount)` on that original transaction. It throws `UnknownReceiptError` if the receipt doesn't exist.
- **R-REFUND-LIMIT**: a refund can't exceed what is left on the original charge. Refunds above 500.00 per account per UTC day need a second approval. The method calls `checkRefundLimit` and tracks running totals per charge and per account per day. It also rolls the totals back if the gateway call fails. This requirement is marked **risk-relevant**. It controls **RISK-REFUND-ABUSE**: "a compromised account or a mistaken operator drains funds through refunds."
- **R-AUDIT-MONEY**: every charge and refund appends an audit entry. The method appends one with `action: "refund"` after the gateway call succeeds.

## Tests that cover it
All the links below are currently in the `valid` state.

- `src/refunds.test.ts#Refunder > refunds to the original transaction` verifies R-REFUND-ORIGINAL and R-AUDIT-MONEY.
- `src/refunds.test.ts#Refunder > totals refunds per account and UTC day` verifies R-REFUND-LIMIT. It exercises the daily total through `refund`.
- `src/refunds.test.ts#checkRefundLimit` verifies R-REFUND-LIMIT. It tests the limit helper directly, not `refund` itself.
- `src/payments.test.ts#Processor > appends an audit entry` verifies R-AUDIT-MONEY. It is about the charge path, so it only covers `refund` indirectly.

## Gaps
- No test is linked for the rollback when the gateway fails.
- No test is linked for `UnknownReceiptError`.

Either might exist in the test file without a trace link. I didn't read `src/refunds.test.ts`, so I can't say.

Because R-REFUND-LIMIT is risk-relevant, I'd need to ask you before changing that code.
